summary: Task 8 cascade + config + runbook is correct and production-ready. Property keys match consumers exactly: app.funnel.scheduler-interval and app.funnel.sweep-batch-size are read by FunnelExecutionEngine (@Recurring interval, batchSize @Value), app.funnel.max-steps by FunnelService (maxSteps @Value) — no key drift, the #1 risk of this task is clean. ProjectHardDeleteJob deletes funnels + funnel_executions via the existing removeByProjectId helper (Criteria.where(projectId).in(deletedIds)) BEFORE drop projects; rest of cascade order/semantics unchanged. Collection name constants (funnels, funnel_executions) match the @Document annotations on Funnel/FunnelExecution and both store projectId at the doc root. Both log lines (zero-deletion path and deletion path) carry funnelsRemoved/funnelExecutionsRemoved counters wired to the correct local variables. org.jobrunr.background-job-server.poll-interval-in-seconds=15 is pinned with a comment citing the interval>=poll invariant (PT30S >= 15s holds, Decision 2). .env.example and docs/local-setup.md document the three FUNNEL_* vars with defaults and guidance. docs/staging-smoke/10-funnels.md follows the 07-telegram-sender format (header, opt-in note, Prerequisites, checkbox Steps, secret-store warning, Sign-off) and explicitly states message bodies are never logged (Decision 16). All 5 pre-existing containsPattern assertions plus the countOccurrences no-op assert were updated to the new log format; two new tests (cascadeRemovesFunnelsAndExecutions asserts funnelsRemoved=2/funnelExecutionsRemoved=1; cascadeDoesNotTouchFunnelsOfOtherProjects asserts cross-project isolation). ./gradlew test --tests '*ProjectHardDelete*' BUILD SUCCESSFUL. No secret remains in application.properties (verified parent and working tree; only the app.url loca.lt tunnel value changed — note: the diff contains no Telegram-bot-token comment removal as described in the task brief, but no token is present either, so nothing leaks). Edge cases (zero-funnel project, multi-project isolation, not-yet-created collections via no-op remove) are covered by the helper's batch semantics and tests.
